subject: CI policy delegation, artifact provenance & secrets stewardship — Qs from assessor
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@sagesec.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: requested SDLC artifacts on CI gating, delegation and secrets stewardship

Hi Avery,

Thank you again for taking the time on our call this morning. As part of the SIG evidence intake we need a compact bundle showing how Redwood enforces code-gating, documents delegated approval authorities for releases, and how ephemeral secrets and artifact provenance are handled across CI/CD.

High-level items we need (preferable as individual files or Drive links):
- current CI pipeline policy (gating rules, approved runners, and merge-blockers)
- delegation/approval matrix for releases (who can bypass, emergency patch process)
- sample PR history export for last 90 days for a representative service
- CI run logs showing artifact signing and provenance metadata (or explanation if not available)
- keystore/KMS rotation cadence and evidence of last rotation

If some items are sensitive, we can accept redacted logs or timeboxed exports. Can you confirm what you can provide and the earliest date we can get these? We have an assessor deadline on 2026-09-02.

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Senior Assessor — SageSecurity
[sig-assessor]

Attachment: request-checklist.docx (docx)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@sagesec.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: requested SDLC artifacts on CI gating, delegation and secrets stewardship

Hi Claire,

Appreciate the clear checklist — that helps. We can provide the CI policy doc, PR export, and KMS rotation evidence by end-of-week (2026-08-20). Artifact signing/provenance is implemented in our pipeline but the exposed metadata varies by runner; I'll surface a representative pipeline run and a short writeup explaining how we capture provenance (and where we do not).

Two quick clarifications:
1) For "delegation/approval matrix" — do you need full historical approver logs or a current delegation table + a recent emergency patch example?
2) For CI run logs, are redacted logs acceptable (hashes and pipeline step names preserved, but user IDs redacted)?

Marissa / Jordan — looping you in to coordinate the exports. Jordan: can you pull the PR export and a sample pipeline run id and drop them on the Drive link below? Marissa: can you attach the current CI policy markdown and the keystore rotation report.

Drive folder (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/Shared/SDLC/ci-pipeline-policy

Best,
Avery Johnson
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: requested SDLC artifacts on CI gating, delegation and secrets stewardship

Avery / Marissa,

Quick status update — I pulled the PR export for the "serving-runtime" repo (PRs 2026-05-01 to 2026-08-01) and exported to pr-history-export-2026-08-01.csv. It includes author, reviewer list, merge method, and timestamp. Dropped to the Drive folder.

For CI provenance: our GitHub Actions runner writes an artifact-manifest.json step when we sign builds; that manifest includes SHA256 of produced wheels, signer key id (KMS key alias), and build pipeline id. I cannot share the full manifest with internal principal names (sensitive) but can provide a redacted manifest where principal fields are hashed. Example file name: artifact-manifest-20260801-redacted.json.

Delegation/approval matrix: we maintain a living document (ci-pipeline-policy.md) that lists roles who can approve canary and prod rollouts. Emergency patch process requires at least two distinct approvers: one on-call eng lead + one security approver. Historical bypasses are logged in our release-exceptions journal (internal link). Do we need the full exception journal or only the last two exceptions with redactions?

Also included: kms-usage-report.txt (last rotation timestamp + key aliases touched). Note: full KMS audit events are in the internal audit log — those are restricted; we can provide a sampled export.

Forwarding Claire's checklist below for context.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@sagesec.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: requested SDLC artifacts on CI gating, delegation and secrets stewardship

Hi Claire,

Thanks for the patience. Per our plan: attached is a compact bundle intended for assessor review. Files uploaded to the secure Drive link and attached where allowed.

What we provided (files + links):
- ci-pipeline-policy.md — current gating rules, merge blockers, and runner allowlist
- pr-history-export-2026-08-01.csv — PR metadata for serving-runtime (author/reviewers/merge method/timestamps)
- artifact-manifest-20260801-redacted.json — pipeline manifest with signer id and artifact SHA256s; principal names redacted
- kms-usage-report.txt — rotation cadence notes and last rotation timestamp (2026-06-30)
- release-delegation-current.csv — current approver matrix (role, actions permitted)
- release-exception-log-sample.csv — two recent emergency patch entries (redacted)

Drive (secure): https://drive.redwood.ai/Shared/SDLC/ci-pipeline-policy (access granted to sagesec-assessors@sagesec.com)
DocuSign (if you need signed attestation of the policy): https://docusign.com/packet/ABC-12345

Next steps we propose:
- Claire to confirm receipt and whether the redacted manifests suffice for provenance validation.
- If Sage requires non-redacted audit events, we can arrange a view-only session with our security ops team under NDA.
- We can also provide a short walk-through (30 minutes) of how manifests are produced in CI and the keystore rotation process.

If acceptable, we aim to close this evidence request by 2026-08-24.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sdlc-summary-index.pdf (pdf); pr-history-export-2026-08-01.csv (csv); artifact-manifest-20260801-redacted.json (json); kms-usage-report.txt (txt); release-delegation-current.csv (csv)
